meta.landing-description: Which hotels ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Claude actually recommend, city by city. Public methodology, free data.
meta.methodology-description: The prompts, the models, the cadence and the AI Visibility Score behind the RankHotel.ai observatory.
meta.city-description: The ranking of the hotels in {city} most recommended by AI models, the sources AI cites, and how much of that traffic ends up on OTAs.

wip.title: Data in progress
wip.body: The rankings below are a demonstration sample, generated to show what the observatory will look like. They are not measured on the models yet: daily collection is being switched on. That's why these pages are not indexed.

landing.title: Which hotels AI really recommends, city by city
landing.lead: A traveler asking «best hotels in Florence» gets an answer with a handful of names in it. Those names are worth bookings. We measure who makes the list, how often and in which position, and publish it with no paywall.

cities.title: Cities we monitor
cities.body: Starting with the major Italian cities. Open a city to see the ranking, the sources AI cites and how much weight the OTAs carry.

example.title: An example: {city}
example.body: This is how a city page reads: first who gets recommended, then where AI takes its information from.

italy.title: The Italian picture
italy.body: Across cities we compare only what is comparable: how much weight OTAs carry ({ota} on average), how much the models agree, how concentrated the ranking is on the top three.
italy.leaderboard-body: Ranked by their place within their own city, not by absolute score: a 90 in Rome and a 90 in Verona are not the same thing.

co-mentions.legend: Numbers are a percentage of answers: the most frequent pair shows up together in {share} of them.

city.title: Hotel AI visibility in {city}
city.lead: Who AI models recommend to someone looking for a hotel in {city}, from which sources, and how much of that traffic ends up on OTAs.

metrics.ota-hint: citations pointing to Booking and the like
metrics.agreement-hint: how similar the models' top 5 are

ranking.title: Who AI recommends
ranking.body: The score combines how often a hotel is cited and in which position. «Presence» is the share of answers it appears in.

citations.title: Where AI takes its information from
citations.body: Every answer cites sources. Here {ota} of them go to OTAs: that's the slice of bookings passing through an intermediary instead of the hotel's own site.

co-mentions.title: Who shows up with whom
co-mentions.body: When AI names a hotel, which others does it name in the same answer. That's the real competitor map: not the one you assume, the one the model puts you next to.

intents.title: The questions that count
intents.body: Not every question is worth the same. Someone asking where to book is closer to the credit card than someone looking for ideas.

movements.title: What changed
movements.body: Movements in the latest window: who entered, who overtook whom, who slipped out.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.lead: Transparency is part of the product. Here's exactly how we produce the observatory data.

models.title: The {count} models
models.body: We query {list}. Claude is included by default: many tools treat it as an option on request, we don't.

prompts.title: The {count} prompts
prompts.body: For each city we ask the same {count} prompts, half in Italian and half in English, every day. They cover the full discovery range: from the generic query to high-intent niches. No prompt contains a hotel name — we measure what the model picks on its own.

cadence.title: The cadence
cadence.body: Every prompt is asked once a day to each model: {prompts} × {models} = {responses} answers per day per city. Published metrics aggregate a rolling window of {days} days. Daily history cannot be reconstructed after the fact: that's what makes the observatory unique over time.

score.title: The AI Visibility Score
score.body: For each hotel we combine two signals: mention frequency (how many answers it appears in) and average position (how high it is cited). The score is normalised 0–100 and weights frequency at {mentionWeight}% and position at {positionWeight}%. We also publish model agreement and the share of direct vs OTA links.

fairness.title: Transparency and fairness
items: Rankings reflect the models' answers, not our judgement of the hotels.
The data is freely citable with attribution to RankHotel.ai.
A hotel can request corrections or removal by writing to hello@rankhotel.ai.
